claims.text: Increasing chemical disorder at multilayer interfaces raises local energy barriers to dislocation nucleation.
Increasing chemical disorder at multilayer interfaces raises local energy barriers to dislocation motion.
The increased barriers caused by interfacial chemical disorder reduce the overall creep strain rate.
The degree of chemical disorder at nanostructured multilayer interfaces can be tuned while bulk composition and layer thickness remain fixed.
Substrate temperature, deposition rate, or post-deposition annealing can be used to vary interfacial chemical disorder while maintaining constant bulk composition and layer periodicity.
Time-dependent deformation of HEAs can be dominated by dislocation-mediated mechanisms under suitable temperature and stress conditions.
Dislocation climb is an active deformation mechanism in the proposed creep-test regime.
Interface sliding is an active deformation mechanism in the proposed creep-test regime.
Enhanced interfacial chemical disorder impedes dislocation climb.
Enhanced interfacial chemical disorder impedes interface sliding.
Dislocation climb and interface sliding are critical contributors to creep deformation in these multilayer coatings.
More chemically disordered interfaces will produce a significantly lower creep strain rate than relatively ordered interfaces under identical test conditions.
More chemically disordered interfaces will extend creep lifetime relative to relatively ordered interfaces.
Atomic diffusion contributes to creep in the applicable temperature and stress regime.
Phase transformations can override the effects of multilayer interfaces on creep.
The quantitative reduction in creep strain rate depends on the extent of induced interfacial disorder and on test conditions.
High-resolution TEM and atom-probe tomography can distinguish the proposed high-disorder and relatively ordered interfaces.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant decrease in creep strain rate or increase in creep lifetime in the high-disorder coatings would falsify the hypothesis.
Comparable interfacial dislocation activity in the high-disorder and ordered coatings would falsify the proposed mechanism.
